BURSEVI:v5p233#3/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p233#3/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p233#3/r1.claim: The Prophet, together with the believers who follow him, is commanded to tell the unbelievers about the greatest losers in deeds.
BURSEVI:v5p233#3/r1.anchor: نخبركم أنا ومن تبعني من المؤمنين أيها الكفرة

BURSEVI:v5p233#3/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p233#3/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p233#3/r2.claim: أخسرين أعمالا is an accusative of specification; its plural signals varied kinds of deeds and means the greatest loss among creatures.
BURSEVI:v5p233#3/r2.anchor: نصب على التمييز والجمع للإيذان بتنوعها

BURSEVI:v5p233#3/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p233#3/r3.speaker: الإرشاد
BURSEVI:v5p233#3/r3.claim: Al-Irshad reads this as unbelievers whose deeds were good in themselves, such as charity and freeing slaves, and who proudly expected reward from them.
BURSEVI:v5p233#3/r3.anchor: قال في "الإرشاد" : هذا بيان حال الكفرة باعتبار ما صدر عنهم

SULAMI:v1p418#2/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p418#2/r1.speaker: أبو بكر الوراق
SULAMI:v1p418#2/r1.claim: People ruin their good works by reproaching recipients and demanding thanks, and ruin worship by performing it for show and reputation.
SULAMI:v1p418#2/r1.anchor: قال أبو بكر الوراق : حين سئل عن هذه الآية قال : هو الذي يبطل معروفه في الدنيا مع أهلها بالمنة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p230/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p230/r1.speaker: علي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p230/r1.claim: Ali identifies the greatest losers as monks, by analogy with the “toiling, weary” phrase.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p230/r1.anchor: عن علي هم الرهبان كقوله عاملة ناصبة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p230/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p230/r2.speaker: مجاهد، author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p230/r2.claim: Mujahid says the People of the Book; other views say the Sabians or, in Ali's answer to Ibn al-Kawwa, the Harurites. The author treats these as examples, not an exhaustive definition: the label covers those outside Islam, show-offs, and heretics whose innovations lead to unbelief.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p230/r2.anchor: وعن مجاهد: هم أهل الكتاب. وقيل: هم الصابئون

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p230/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p230/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p230/r4.claim: Alladhīna may be nominative as the predicate of an omitted “they are,” or accusative for censure; the next clause can then be its description or apposition.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p230/r4.anchor: والذين يصح رفعه على أنه خبر مبتدأ محذوف، أي هم الذين

ALUSI-FULL:v16p47#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p47#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p47#2/r1.claim: The question addresses unbelievers; if read as seeking their leave to announce the news, it is deeply sarcastic.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p47#2/r1.anchor: خطاب للكفرة وإذا حمل الإستفهام على الاستئذان كان فيه من التهكم

ALUSI-FULL:v16p47#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p47#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p47#2/r2.claim: The plural “we” either immediately identifies the speaker or signals that believers already know this news as well.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p47#2/r2.anchor: قيل لتعيينه من أول الأمر وللإيذان بمعلومية النبأ للمؤمنين أيضا

ALUSI-FULL:v16p47#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p47#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p47#2/r3.claim: أعمالا is an accusative specification; it is plural because it means “workers,” whereas a source noun used as specification can remain singular.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p47#2/r3.anchor: أما إذا كان مؤولا بإسم فاعل فإنه يعامل معاملته وهنا عمل بمعنى عامل

ALUSI-FULL:v16p47#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p47#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p47#2/r4.claim: An alternative says أعمالا is a rare plural of عامل; some grammarians deny such plurals outside a few established words.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p47#2/r4.anchor: وزعم بعضهم أن أعمالا جمع عامل وتعقب بأن جمع فاعل على أفعال نادر

ALUSI-FULL:v16p47#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p47#2/r5.speaker: القاموس
ALUSI-FULL:v16p47#2/r5.claim: Another proposal treats أعمالا as plural of عمل, meaning people possessed of deeds; the author finds this strained.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p47#2/r5.anchor: جمع عمل ككتف بمعنى ذو عمل

ALUSI-FULL:v16p47#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p47#2/r6.speaker: إرشاد العقل السليم
ALUSI-FULL:v16p47#2/r6.claim: The passage contrasts unbelievers’ intrinsically good acts, which they admire and expect reward for, with their intrinsically bad acts that they mistakenly deem good.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p47#2/r6.anchor: بيان لحال الكفرة باعتبار ما صدر عنهم من الأعمال الحسنة في أنفسها

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p210#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p210#2/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p210#2/r1.claim: The greatest losers exhaust themselves in work expecting reward but end in ruin, like a merchant who buys expecting profit and loses.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p210#2/r1.anchor: يعني: الذين أتعبوا أنفسهم في عمل يرجون به فضلا ونوالا فنالوا هلاكا وبوارا كمن يشتري سلعة يرجو عليها ربحا

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p210#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p210#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس وسعد بن أبي وقاص
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p210#2/r2.claim: They identify the losers as Jews and Christians.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p210#2/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس وسعد بن أبي وقاص: هم اليهود والنصارى.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p210#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p210#2/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p210#2/r3.claim: Another view identifies them as monks who confined themselves to monasteries.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p210#2/r3.anchor: وقيل: هم الرهبان. {الذين} حبسوا أنفسهم في الصوامع.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p210#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p210#2/r4.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p210#2/r4.claim: He identifies them as the people of Ḥarūrāʾ.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p210#2/r4.anchor: وقال علي بن أبي طالب: هم أهل حروراء

BAYDAWI-FULL:18:103/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:103/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:103/r1.claim: The accusative aʿmālan is a specification; it is plural because it modifies active agents or because their deeds are diverse.
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:103/r1.anchor: نصب على التمييز وجمع لأنه من أسماء الفاعلين أو لتنوع أعمالهم

NAHHAS:v2p475/r6.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p475/r6.speaker: حمزة
NAHHAS:v2p475/r6.claim: The author judges Hamza’s reading more correct, following Sibawayh’s concern about assimilating lām into nūn, although that assimilation is possible at a distance because the articulation points are close.
NAHHAS:v2p475/r6.anchor: وقراءة حمزة أصوب وأولى في هذا ، وهذا قول سيبويه ؛ لأنه يستبعد أن تدغم اللام في النون

NAHHAS:v2p475/r7.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p475/r7.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p475/r7.claim: ‘The greatest losers in deeds’ uses an accusative of specification.

BIQAI-FULL:v4p509/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p509/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p509/r1.claim: Muhammad is told to warn those heedless of remembrance, whose eyes and ears fail to take in the warning, about the greatest losers.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p509/r1.anchor: إخبارا عظيما أيها التاركون من لا خالق ولا رازق لهم سواه

BIQAI-FULL:v4p509/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p509/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p509/r2.claim: Their deeds vary: some worship angels, stars, prophets, or idols, while others commit different forms of unbelief.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p509/r2.anchor: فمنهم من يعبد الملائكة , ومنهم من يعبد النجوم

BIQAI-FULL:v4p509/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p509/r5.speaker: سعد بن أبي وقاص
BIQAI-FULL:v4p509/r5.claim: Al-Bukhārī transmits from Saʿd that the greatest losers are Jews and Christians: Jews rejected Muhammad, while Christians denied Paradise has food or drink.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p509/r5.anchor: وروى البخاري في التفسير عن سعد بن أبي وقاص رضي الله عنه أن الأخسرين اليهود والنصارى

BIQAI-FULL:v4p509/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p509/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p509/r6.claim: The author adds that both groups deny bodily resurrection and restrict the afterlife to a spiritual one.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p509/r6.anchor: وكذا قال اليهود لأن الفريقين أنكروا الحشر الجسماني وخصوه بالروحاني

DURR-FULL:v5p463/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p463/r7.speaker: سعد
DURR-FULL:v5p463/r7.claim: Sa'd rejects identifying the greatest losers as the Kharijites and instead names Jews and Christians: Jews rejected Muhammad, Christians denied food and drink in Paradise, while Kharijites break God's covenant and were called transgressors.
DURR-FULL:v5p463/r7.anchor: من طريق مصعب بن سعد قال: سألت أبي {قل هل ننبئكم بالأخسرين أعمالا} أهم الحرورية قال: لا هم اليهود والنصارى

DURR-FULL:v5p463/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p463/r8.speaker: سعد
DURR-FULL:v5p463/r8.claim: In another report Sa'd names monastic ascetics and the Kharijites as people who strayed, whereupon God caused their hearts to stray.
DURR-FULL:v5p463/r8.anchor: أصحاب الصوامع والحرورية قوم زاغوا فأزاغ الله قلوبهم

DURR-FULL:v5p465/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p465/r1.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
DURR-FULL:v5p465/r1.claim: Ali identifies the greatest losers as monks who confined themselves to pillars.
DURR-FULL:v5p465/r1.anchor: عن أبي خميصة عبد الله بن قيس قال: سمعت علي بن أبي طالب يقول في هذه الآية {قل هل ننبئكم بالأخسرين أعمالا} إنهم الرهبان

DURR-FULL:v5p465/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p465/r2.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
DURR-FULL:v5p465/r2.claim: When Ibn al-Kawwa asked, Ali identified the greatest losers as Quraysh's transgressors.
DURR-FULL:v5p465/r2.anchor: عن أبي الطفيل قال: سمعت علي بن أبي طالب وسأله ابن الكواء فقال: من {هل ننبئكم بالأخسرين أعمالا} قال: فجرة قريش

DURR-FULL:v5p465/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p465/r3.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
DURR-FULL:v5p465/r3.claim: Ali also thought the Kharijites were included among those described as the greatest losers.
DURR-FULL:v5p465/r3.anchor: عن علي أنه سئل عن هذه الآية {قل هل ننبئكم بالأخسرين أعمالا} قال: لا أظن إلا أن الخوارج منهم

DURR-FULL:v5p465/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p465/r5.speaker: كعب
DURR-FULL:v5p465/r5.claim: Ka'b says the Quran appears as a beautiful, fragrant companion to the person who acted by it, soothes his terror, and identifies itself as his good deeds.
DURR-FULL:v5p465/r5.anchor: عن كعب قال: يمثل القرآن لمن كان يعمل به في الدنيا يوم القيامة كأحسن صورة رآها وجها أحسنه وأطيبه ريحا

DURR-FULL:v5p465/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p465/r6.speaker: كعب
DURR-FULL:v5p465/r6.claim: The Quran asks God to intercede for its companion, reminding Him that it occupied his days with thirst and nights with wakefulness; he is then crowned and robed in honor.
DURR-FULL:v5p465/r6.anchor: طالما اظمأت نهاره وأسهرت ليله فشفعني فيه فيوضع تاج الملك على رأسه ويكسى حلة الملك

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p45/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p45/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p45/r1.claim: The passage answers those who worship useless idols as patrons and seek their favor, making their work and effort futile; the key rebuke is that they think they do well.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p45/r1.anchor: فإنهم لما اتخذوا أولياء من ليسوا ينفعونهم فاختاروا الأصنام وعبدوها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p45/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p45/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p45/r2.claim: Beginning with the command say signals an important utterance deserving attentive listening.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p45/r2.anchor: وافتتاح الجملة بالأمر بالقول للاهتمام بالمقول بإصغاء السامعين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p45/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p45/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p45/r3.claim: The question whether to inform them is an offer used ironically: the speaker will inform them regardless of their assent.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p45/r3.anchor: وكذلك افتتاحه باستفهامهم عن إنبائهم استفهاما مستعملا في العرض لأنه بمعنى : أتحبون أن ننبئكم بالأخسرين أعمالا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p45/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p45/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p45/r4.claim: The wording shifts from direct address to third person, building curiosity before revealing that the losers are the listeners themselves.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p45/r4.anchor: وفي قوله { بالأخسرين أعمالا } إلى آخره . . . تمليح إذ عدل فيه عن طريقة الخطاب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p45/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p45/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p45/r5.claim: The polytheists are addressed to rebuke them and alert them to the failure of their efforts.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p45/r5.anchor: والمقول لهم : المشركون ، توبيخا لهم وتنبيها على ما غفلوا عنه من خيبة سعيهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p45/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p45/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p45/r6.claim: The plural nūn in nunabbiʾukum may be God’s majestic plural, with narrative shift from expected he informs you.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p45/r6.anchor: يجوز أن تكون نون العظمة راجعة إلى ذات الله على طريقة الالتفات

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p45/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p45/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p45/r7.claim: Alternatively, the plural nūn may refer to the Messenger together with God, or to the Messenger and Muslims.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p45/r7.anchor: ويجوز أن تكون راجعة للرسول وللمسلمين

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p544#3/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p544#3/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p544#3/r6.claim: The question about the greatest losers is a taunting rebuke addressed to the disbelievers.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p544#3/r6.anchor: ثم قال تعالى: هل ننبئكم بالأخسرين أعمالا الآية المعنى: قل لهؤلاء الكفرة على جهة التوبيخ

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p197#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p197#2/r1.speaker: علي والضحاك
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p197#2/r1.claim: One view identifies the worst losers as Christian priests and monks.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p197#2/r1.anchor: أحدهما أنهم القسيسون والرهبان قاله علي عليه السلام والضحاك

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p197#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p197#2/r2.speaker: سعد بن أبي وقاص
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p197#2/r2.claim: Another view identifies them as Jews and Christians.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p197#2/r2.anchor: والثاني اليهود والنصارى قاله سعد بن أبي وقاص

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p197#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p197#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p197#2/r3.claim: أعمالا is an accusative specification: الأخسرين alone leaves unclear what was lost, so أعمالا names the kind of loss.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p197#2/r3.anchor: أعمالا منصوب على التمييز لأنه لما قال بالأخسرين كان ذلك مبهما

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p201#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p201#2/r1.speaker: سعد بن أبي وقاص
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p201#2/r1.claim: Asked whether the greatest losers are the Haruriyya, Sa'd answers that they are Jews and Christians: Jews rejected Muhammad, while Christians denied food and drink in Paradise; the Haruriyya break God's covenant after pledging it, and Sa'd called them profligates. Bukhari transmits this.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p201#2/r1.anchor: سألت أبي -يعني سعد بن أبي وقاص-: {قل هل ننبئكم بالأخسرين أعمالا} أهم الحرورية؟ قال: لا هم اليهود والنصارى

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p201#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p201#2/r2.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب والضحاك
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p201#2/r2.claim: Ali, al-Dahhak, and others identify the greatest losers as the Haruriyya.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p201#2/r2.anchor: وقال علي بن أبي طالب (1) والضحاك، وغير واحد: هم الحرورية.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p201#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p201#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p201#2/r3.claim: The verse broadly includes the Haruriyya alongside Jews, Christians, and others; it is not exclusive to any group, since it is Meccan, before the relevant Jewish-Christian address and before the Khawarij existed. It covers anyone who follows an unapproved way while thinking the work is accepted, as echoed in 88:2–4, 25:23, and 24:39.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p201#2/r3.anchor: أن هذه الآية الكريمة تشمل الحرورية كما تشمل اليهود والنصارى وغيرهم، لا أنها نزلت في هؤلاء على الخصوص

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p201#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p201#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p201#2/r4.claim: The greatest losers are those whose efforts were invalid under a lawful, pleasing religious way, yet who believe they are doing well and that their deeds are accepted and loved.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p201#2/r4.anchor: أي: عملوا أعمالا باطلة على غير شريعة مشروعة مرضية مقبولة

JISHUMI:v6p4501/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4501/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4501/r1.claim: The passage affirms Gog and Magog and the trumpet blast as signs of the Hour.
JISHUMI:v6p4501/r1.anchor: خروج يأجوج ومأجوج، والنفخ في الصور، وكل ذلك من أشراط الساعة

JISHUMI:v6p4503/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4503/r3.speaker: علي
JISHUMI:v6p4503/r3.claim: A report says the verse about the greatest losers was revealed concerning monks and priests who confined themselves in monasteries.
JISHUMI:v6p4503/r3.anchor: قيل: نزل قوله: (الأخسرين أعمالا) في الرهبان والقسيسين الذين حبسوا أنفسهم

JISHUMI:v6p4503/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4503/r4.speaker: سعد بن أبي وقاص، ابن عباس
JISHUMI:v6p4503/r4.claim: Another report identifies the greatest losers as Jews and Christians.
JISHUMI:v6p4503/r4.anchor: وقيل: في اليهود والنصارى، عن سعد بن أبي وقاص، وابن عباس

JISHUMI:v6p4503/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4503/r5.speaker: أبو علي
JISHUMI:v6p4503/r5.claim: Abu Ali reports that it was revealed concerning the people of Haruraʾ.
JISHUMI:v6p4503/r5.anchor: وقيل: نزل في أهل حروراء، عن أبي علي

JISHUMI:v6p4503/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4503/r6.speaker: الأصم
JISHUMI:v6p4503/r6.claim: Al-Asamm strongly rejects the Haruriyya report because the verse calls them unbelievers in God's signs while they are Muslims.
JISHUMI:v6p4503/r6.anchor: وأنكر الأصم ذلك أشد الإنكار، واستدل بقوله: (أولئك الذين كفروا بآيات ربهم)

JISHUMI:v6p4503/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4503/r7.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4503/r7.claim: If the report from Ali is authentic, it must be accepted; kufr here can mean rejecting some of God's signs, as rebels do.
JISHUMI:v6p4503/r7.anchor: قلنا: إن صح ذلك عن علي (عليه السلام) فلا بد من قبوله

JISHUMI:v6p4503/r13.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4503/r13.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4503/r13.claim: Those who assume worship of others benefits them are the greatest losers: they exhaust themselves in deeds they think right, then end in the Fire.
JISHUMI:v6p4503/r13.anchor: أكثر خسرانا على تحملهم لأنهم أتعبوا أنفسهم في أعمالهم ظنا أنهم على شيء

SAMIN-DURR:18:103/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:103/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:18:103/r1.claim: أعمالا is a specification of الأخسرين and is plural because the kinds of deeds differ.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p347/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p347/r1.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p347/r1.claim: The worst in deeds are priests and monks.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p347/r1.anchor: خسمة أقاويل : أحدها : أنهم القسيسون والرهبان

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p347/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p347/r2.speaker: سعد بن أبي وقاص
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p347/r2.claim: They are Jews and Christians among the People of the Book.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p347/r2.anchor: الثاني : أنهم الكتابيون اليهود والنصارى , قاله سعد بن أبي وقاص

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p347/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p347/r3.speaker: علي
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p347/r3.claim: Another report identifies them as the people of Harura, the Kharijites.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p347/r3.anchor: الثالث : هم أهل حروراء من الخوارج , وهذا مروي عن علي رضي الله عنه

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p347/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p347/r4.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p347/r4.claim: Another interpretation identifies them as followers of religious whims.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p347/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p347/r5.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p347/r5.claim: Another interpretation is people who do good deeds and boast of them.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p347/r5.anchor: الخامس : أنهم من يصطنع المعروف ويمن عليه

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p347/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p347/r6.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p347/r6.claim: Possible referents are hypocrites whose deeds contradict belief, or people who seek this world and abandon the next.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p347/r6.anchor: ويحتمل سادسا : أنهم المنافقون بأعمالهم المخالفون باعتقادهم

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p347/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p347/r7.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p347/r7.claim: A further possible referent is those who seek this world and abandon the next.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p347/r7.anchor: ويحتمل سابعا : أنهم طالبو الدنيا وتاركو الآخرة

MUQATIL:18:103-107/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:18:103-107/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:18:103-107/r1.claim: The greatest losers in deeds are the Christian monks living in cells.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p28#4/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p28#4/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p28#4/r1.claim: A plural tamyīz is used where singular would be expected to express the many kinds of desires; the referents are the People of the Book or monks.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p28#4/r1.anchor: اعمالا تمييز وإنما جمع والقياس ان يكون مفردا لتنوع الاهواء وهم اهل الكتاب

QURTUBI-FULL:18:99-105/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:99-105/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:18:99-105/r9.claim: The verses show that people may work while imagining their deeds good even though their effort is nullified; the cause is corrupt belief or ostentation, and here specifically disbelief.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:99-105/r9.anchor: فيه دلالة على أن من الناس من يعمل العمل وهو يظن أنه محسن وقد حبط سعيه

QURTUBI-FULL:18:99-105/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:99-105/r10.speaker: سعد
QURTUBI-FULL:18:99-105/r10.claim: In a Bukhari report, Saʿd says the worst losers are Jews and Christians, not the Khawarij: Jews denied Muhammad, and Christians denied Paradise’s food and drink; he called the Khawarij covenant-breakers and wicked.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:99-105/r10.anchor: أهم الحرورية؟ قال: لا هم اليهود والنصارى

QURTUBI-FULL:18:99-105/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:99-105/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:18:99-105/r11.claim: The question rebukes disbelievers who worship other than God: their efforts and hopes fail, making them the greatest losers in deeds.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:99-105/r11.anchor: الآية معناها التوبيخ أي قل لهؤلاء الكفرة الذين عبدوا غيري

QURTUBI-FULL:18:99-105/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:99-105/r13.speaker: علي
QURTUBI-FULL:18:99-105/r13.claim: Ali identifies the worst losers as the Khawarij of Harura; on another occasion he names the monks in their cells, and tells Ibn al-Kawwa that he and his companions are meant.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:99-105/r13.anchor: وقال علي: هم الخوارج أهل حروراء. وقال مرة: هم الرهبان أصحاب الصوامع

QURTUBI-FULL:18:99-105/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:99-105/r14.speaker: ابن عطية
QURTUBI-FULL:18:99-105/r14.claim: Ibn Atiyya says these identifications are weakened by the following description of people who disbelieved God’s signs and meeting Him; that fits Meccan idolaters, though Ali and Saʿd named groups that share aspects of the warning.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:99-105/r14.anchor: فحبطت أعمالهم } وليس من هذه الطوائف من يكفر بالله ولقائه

ZAJJAJ:v3p314/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p314/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p314/r1.claim: أعمالا is a specification after الأخسرين, clarifying the type of loss.
ZAJJAJ:v3p314/r1.anchor: منصوب على التمييز لأنه إذ قال: (بالأخسرين)، دل على أنه كان منهم

STUDYQURAN:18:103/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:18:103/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:18:103/r1.claim: The greatest losers are those who disbelieve in God’s signs and meeting Him, because their worldly efforts are futile.
STUDYQURAN:18:103/r1.anchor: Those who disbelieve in the signs of their Lord, and in the meeting with Him (v. 105) are described in this passage as the greatest losers

TABATABAI:18:103-105/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:103-105/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:103-105/r1.claim: These six verses draw a conclusion from the sūrah’s account of worldly seduction, reliance on protectors besides God, spiritual blindness, and bad outcomes, and prepare for the closing declaration at 18:110.
TABATABAI:18:103-105/r1.anchor: بيان الآيات الست في منزلة الاستنتاج مما تقدم من آيات السورة

TABATABAI:18:103-105/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:103-105/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:103-105/r2.claim: The indirect address in “shall We inform you” targets polytheists, made explicit by the later description of those who disbelieved in God’s signs and meeting Him; the plural “deeds” stresses their varied losses.
TABATABAI:18:103-105/r2.anchor: ظاهر السياق أن الخطاب للمشركين وهو مسوق سوق الكناية

TABRISI:18:99-105/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:99-105/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:18:99-105/r7.claim: The greatest losers in works are disbelieving Jews and Christians whose efforts in worldly life came to nothing while they thought their actions were virtuous acts of obedience and worship.
TABRISI:18:99-105/r7.anchor: وهم كفار أهل الكتاب اليهود والنصارى

TABRISI:18:99-105/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:99-105/r8.speaker: العياشي
TABRISI:18:99-105/r8.claim: Al-ʿAyyāshī transmits that Ibn al-Kawwa asked Ali about the greatest losers: Ali identified scriptural communities who disbelieved and innovated, adding that the Khawarij were not far from them.
TABRISI:18:99-105/r8.anchor: أولئك أهل الكتاب كفروا بربهم وابتدعوا في دينهم

THALABI:v6p200#2/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p200#2/r1.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
THALABI:v6p200#2/r1.claim: He identifies the greatest losers as monks and priests who confined themselves in cloisters.
THALABI:v6p200#2/r1.anchor: هم الرهبان والقسوس الذين حبسوا أنفسهم في الصوامع

THALABI:v6p200#2/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p200#2/r2.speaker: سعد بن أبي وقاص وابن عباس
THALABI:v6p200#2/r2.claim: They identify them as Jews and Christians, comparing the claim with the description of weary workers entering a blazing fire.
THALABI:v6p200#2/r2.anchor: هم اليهود والنصارى، نظيره: عاملة ناصبة تصلى نارا حامية

THALABI:v6p200#2/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p200#2/r3.speaker: علي
THALABI:v6p200#2/r3.claim: Asked by Ibn al-Kawwa about the greatest losers, he answers that they are the people of Harura, the Kharijites.
THALABI:v6p200#2/r3.anchor: عن قوله: هل ننبئكم بالأخسرين أعمالا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p164/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p164/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p164/r1.claim: The question asks about people whose deeds make them the greatest losers among creation.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p164/r1.anchor: أي: بالقوم الذين هم أخسر الخلق فيما عملوا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p164/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p164/r2.speaker: ابن عباس رواية عطاء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p164/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies them as disbelieving People of the Book.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p164/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس في رواية عطاء: (يرد كفار أهل الكتاب)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p164/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p164/r3.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p164/r3.claim: Al-Kalbi identifies them as Jews and Christians.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p164/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p164/r4.speaker: علي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p164/r4.claim: One report from Ali identifies them as monks living in cells.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p164/r4.anchor: وروي عن علي -رضي الله عنه- أنه قال: (هم الرهبان أصحاب الصوامع) (¬6)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p164/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p164/r5.speaker: علي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p164/r5.claim: Another report from Ali identifies them as the people of Harura, the Kharijites.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p164/r5.anchor: وعنه أيضا أنه قال: (هم أهل حروراء) (¬1)

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p62/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p62/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p62/r1.claim: In Arabic, akhsar means greater loss than khasir, so the comparative form marks a more severe degree of loss.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p62/r1.anchor: وفي اللغة الأخسر هو أكثر خسراناً من الخاسر

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p62/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p62/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p62/r2.claim: The people described in Hud block both themselves and others from God's path, unlike those in Nahl who block only themselves; they are therefore more grievously lost.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p62/r2.anchor: الذي يصدّ نفسه وغيره عن سبيل الله أخسر من الذي صدّ نفسه عن سبيل الله لوحده فقط

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p63/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p63/r1.speaker: النحاة
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p63/r1.claim: Grammarians explain la jarama as an oath, or as meaning truly/rightfully; each reading gives emphasis.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p63/r1.anchor: عند النحاة تعني القسم أو بمعنى حقاً أو حقَّ وكلها تدل على التوكيد

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p63/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p63/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p63/r2.claim: Hud adds several charges beyond Naml, including blocking God's path and lying against God, so it emphatically calls its offenders the worst losers; Naml lacks that added emphasis.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p63/r2.anchor: فقد زاد على ذلك أنهم يصدون عن سبيل الله وأنهم يفترون على الله الكذب

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:18:100-104/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:18:100-104/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:18:100-104/r4.claim: God asks whether people should be told of those whose deeds are most disastrously lost.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:18:100-104/r4.anchor: بالذين هم أشد الخلق وأعظمهم خسرانا فيما عملوا

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p209#2/r5.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p209#2/r5.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p209#2/r5.claim: Hell is prepared for unbelievers; the next question introduces the people who lose most through their deeds.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p209#2/r5.anchor: قال: {إنا أعتدنا جهنم للكافرين نزلا} [الكهف: 102] قوله: {قل هل ننبئكم} [الكهف: 103] يقول: ألا أنبئكم.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p210/r1.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p210/r1.speaker: السدي
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p210/r1.claim: Al-Suddī says the people's effort goes astray, though they think they are doing well; Yaḥyā identifies them as the People of the Book.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p210/r1.anchor: {بالأخسرين أعمالا {103} الذين ضل سعيهم} [الكهف: 103-104] يعني: يضل سعيهم. وهو تفسير السدي.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:103/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:103/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:103/r1.claim: People direct their efforts toward their aims: seeking God’s pleasure and the afterlife leads to one kind of work, while pursuit of worldly gain leads to another.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:103/r1.anchor: İnsanlar, davranışlarında daima bir amaç gözetip ona göre çaba harcarlar.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:103/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:103/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:103/r2.claim: Polytheists think their idols bring them nearer to God and that shirk is obedience, but God gives their deeds no value in this life or the next.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:103/r2.anchor: Allah’a ortak koşanlar tanrılarının kendilerini Allah’a yaklaştıracağını ve Allah katında küfür sayılan bu davranışlarının Allah’a itaat olduğunu sanmaktadırlar.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:103/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:103/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:103/r4.claim: Those who commit the evils described in these verses will be punished in Hell.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:103/r4.anchor: Bunlar âyetlerde belirtilen kötülükleri yaptıkları için cezaları cehennem olacaktır.

JISHUMI:v6p4506/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4506/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4506/r3.claim: The question Will We inform you supports the duty to pursue truth seriously lest one's striving go astray.
JISHUMI:v6p4506/r3.anchor: ويدل قوله: هل ننبئكم على وجوب - التشدد في طلب الحق ليعلمه فلا يضل سعيه

AKHFASH:v2p434/r4.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v2p434/r4.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v2p434/r4.claim: الأخسرين أعمالا is accusative because the article and plural ending prevent annexation, leaving أعمالا as an accusative specification.
AKHFASH:v2p434/r4.anchor: وقال {بالأخسرين أعمالا} لأنه لما ادخل الالف واللام والنون في {الأخسرين} لم يوصل الى الاضافة

TABATABAI:18:108/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:108/r3.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
TABATABAI:18:108/r3.claim: In response to Ibn al-Kawwa’s question about the greatest losers, Ali identifies them as the sinful people of Quraysh.
TABATABAI:18:108/r3.anchor: عن أبي الطفيل قال سمعت علي بن أبي طالب وسأله ابن الكوا فقال

TABATABAI:18:108/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:108/r4.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
TABATABAI:18:108/r4.claim: A report through al-Ayyashi says the losers are People of the Book who disbelieved and innovated; it adds that the people of the River are not far from them.
TABATABAI:18:108/r4.anchor: قام ابن الكوا إلى أمير المؤمنين عليه السلام فقال أخبرني عن قول الله

TABATABAI:18:108/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:108/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:108/r5.claim: The author notes another report identifying the losers as Christians.
TABATABAI:18:108/r5.anchor: أقول وروي أنهم النصاري، القمي عن أبي جعفر

TABATABAI:18:108/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:108/r6.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
TABATABAI:18:108/r6.claim: Al-Qummi and al-Tabarsi transmit that the losers are People of the Book.
TABATABAI:18:108/r6.anchor: القمي عن أبي جعفر عليه السلام والطبرسي في الاحتجاج عن علي عليه السلام أنهم أهل الكتاب

TABATABAI:18:108/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:108/r7.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
TABATABAI:18:108/r7.claim: A report transmitted by Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim identifies them as monks who secluded themselves in pillars.
TABATABAI:18:108/r7.anchor: عن أبي خميصة عبد الله بن قيس عن علي عليه السلام أنهم الرهبان الذين حبسوا أنفسهم في السواري

TABATABAI:18:108/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:108/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:108/r8.claim: These reports are applications rather than the verse’s original referent: the surrounding passage addresses idolaters, and its description in 18:106 fits them better than other groups; al-Qummi’s Jewish-to-Kharijite account is unsound.
TABATABAI:18:108/r8.anchor: والروايات جميعا من قبيل الجري، والآيتان واقعتان في سياق متصل وجه الكلام فيه مع المشركين

THALABI:v6p200/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p200/r8.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p200/r8.claim: The greatest losers are people who tire themselves in work hoping for profit but end in ruin, like a merchant whose investment fails.
THALABI:v6p200/r8.anchor: يعني الذين أتعبوا أنفسهم في عمل يبتغون به ربحا، فنالوا به هلاكا وعطبا،

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p64/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p64/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p64/r1.claim: Sa'y means running or brisk walking; ihsan is mastery rather than ordinary work. Fi'l can describe an inanimate thing, 'amal need not be skilled making, and sun' is finer, intentional work by a rational agent.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p64/r1.anchor: والإحسان هو الإتقان وليس العمل العادي

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p64/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p64/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p64/r2.claim: The verse combines misguidance, striving, and skilled making, so it fittingly says “greatest losers in deeds”; it is the Qur'an's only attribution of loss to work, in a passage framed throughout by deeds.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p64/r2.anchor: جاء فيها ضلال وسعي وصُنع لذا استوجب أن يؤتى بكلمة الأخسرين أعمالاً

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p64/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p64/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p64/r3.claim: Al-akhsarin is a comparative superlative: many are losers, and some are worse than others, so the ranking is among the losers themselves.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p64/r3.anchor: الأخسرين: اسم تفضيل أي أنه هناك اشتراك في الخُسران، يوجد خاسرون كُثُر والأخسرين بعضهم أخسر من بعض

SIBAWAYH:ولمتقوأنتعملعملالفاعللأنهاليستف.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:ولمتقوأنتعملعملالفاعللأنهاليستف.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:ولمتقوأنتعملعملالفاعللأنهاليستف.claim: Sībawayh cites الأَخْسَرِينَ أَعْمَالًا to show a plural adjective with its nūn retained takes an accusative complement, not an iḍāfa or genitive complement.
SIBAWAYH:ولمتقوأنتعملعملالفاعللأنهاليستف.anchor: ومن ذلك قوله تعالى ^ ( قل هل ننبئكم ~~بالأخسرين أعمالا

NASHR:v2p7/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p7/r1.speaker: الكسائي
NASHR:v2p7/r1.claim: Al-Kisai assimilates the lām of hal/ bal into all eight listed consonants, including nūn in هل ننبئكم.
NASHR:v2p7/r1.anchor: وهل ننبئكم فأدغم اللام منهما في الأحرف الثمانية الكسائي

NASHR:v2p7/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p7/r2.speaker: حمزة
NASHR:v2p7/r2.claim: Hamza agrees with al-Kisai on assimilation before tāʾ, thāʾ, and sīn, not before the nūn in this verse.
NASHR:v2p7/r2.anchor: ووافقه حمزة في التاء والثاء، والسين

NASHR:v2p7/r5.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p7/r5.speaker: هشام
NASHR:v2p7/r5.claim: Hisham shows lām before ḍād and nūn, and assimilates it before the other six consonants; the author calls this the sound view followed by most.
NASHR:v2p7/r5.anchor: وأظهرها هشام عند الضاد والنون فقط وأدغمها عند الستة الأحرف الباقية، وهذا هو الصواب والذي عليه الجمهور

NASHR:v2p7/r6.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p7/r6.speaker: أهل الأداء
NASHR:v2p7/r6.claim: Some restrict Hisham’s assimilation to al-Halwani, while al-Ala, al-Dani, and al-Hudhali extend it to both al-Halwani and al-Dajuni routes.
NASHR:v2p7/r6.anchor: خص بعض أهل الأداء الإدغام بالحلواني فقط كذا ذكره أبو طاهر بن سوار

NASHR:v2p7/r7.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p7/r7.speaker: أبو عمرو الداني وأبو القاسم الهذلي
NASHR:v2p7/r7.claim: Al-Dani and al-Hudhali explicitly transmit complete assimilation for Hisham without reporting a disagreement.
NASHR:v2p7/r7.anchor: نص على الإدغام لهشام بكماله الحافظ أبو عمرو الداني في جامع البيان، وأبو القاسم الهذلي في كامله

NASHR:v1p214/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p214/r1.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p214/r1.claim: A reader must articulate each letter at its distinct point of origin and give it its proper qualities through practice until accurate pronunciation becomes natural.
NASHR:v1p214/r1.anchor: تصحيح إخراج كل حرف من مخرجه المختص به تصحيحا يمتاز به عن مقاربه

NASHR:v1p214/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p214/r2.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p214/r2.claim: Letters sharing a point of articulation are distinguished by their qualities; letters sharing qualities are distinguished by their points of articulation.
NASHR:v1p214/r2.anchor: فكل حرف شارك غيره في مخرج، فإنه لا يمتاز عن مشاركه إلا بالصفات

NASHR:v1p214/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p214/r3.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p214/r3.claim: Hamza and hāʾ share articulation, openness, and low tongue position; hamza alone is voiced and a stop.
NASHR:v1p214/r3.anchor: اشتركا مخرجا وانفتاحا واستفالا، وانفردت الهمزة بالجهر والشدة

NASHR:v1p214/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p214/r4.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p214/r4.claim: ʿAyn and ḥāʾ share articulation, openness, and low tongue position; ḥāʾ alone is voiceless and purely fricative.
NASHR:v1p214/r4.anchor: اشتركا مخرجا واستفالا وانفتاحا، وانفردت الحاء بالهمس والرخاوة الخالصة

NASHR:v1p214/r5.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p214/r5.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p214/r5.claim: Ghayn and khāʾ share articulation and several qualities, while ghayn alone is voiced.
NASHR:v1p214/r5.anchor: اشتركا مخرجا ورخاوة واستعلاء وانفتاحا، وانفردت الغين بالجهر

NASHR:v1p214/r6.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p214/r6.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p214/r6.claim: Jīm, shīn, and yāʾ share articulation; jīm is a stop, while shīn is voiceless and spread, and shares softness with yāʾ.
NASHR:v1p214/r6.anchor: اشتركت مخرجا وانفتاحا واستفالا، وانفردت الجيم بالشدة

NASHR:v1p214/r7.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p214/r7.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p214/r7.claim: Ḍād and ẓāʾ share voiced emphatic frication, but differ in articulation; ḍād alone has istiṭāla.
NASHR:v1p214/r7.anchor: اشتركا صفة وجهرا ورخاوة واستعلاء وإطباقا، وافترقا مخرجا، وانفردت الضاد بالاستطالة

NASHR:v1p214/r8.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p214/r8.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p214/r8.claim: Ṭāʾ, dāl, and tāʾ share articulation and stoppage; ṭāʾ is emphatic, dāl voiced, and tāʾ voiceless.
NASHR:v1p214/r8.anchor: اشتركت مخرجا وشدة، وانفردت الطاء بالإطباق والاستعلاء، واشتركت مع الدال

NASHR:v1p214/r9.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p214/r9.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p214/r9.claim: The excerpt compares ẓāʾ, dhāl, and thāʾ by shared articulation and softness, then distinguishes their voicing and emphasis qualities.
NASHR:v1p214/r9.anchor: اشتركت مخرجا ورخاوة وانفردت الطاء بالاستعلاء والإطباق واشتركت مع الذال

NASHR:v1p214/r10.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p214/r10.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p214/r10.claim: Ṣād, zāy, and sīn share articulation, softness, and whistling; ṣād is emphatic, zāy voiced, and sīn voiceless.
NASHR:v1p214/r10.anchor: اشتركت مخرجا ورخاوة وصفيرا وانفردت الصاد بالإطباق والاستعلاء، واشتركت مع السين

NASHR:v1p214/r11.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p214/r11.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p214/r11.claim: Correct isolated letter sounds are insufficient: readers must practice the altered effects that arise when letters are joined to neighbors.
NASHR:v1p214/r11.anchor: فإذا أحكم القارئ النطق بكل حرف على حدته موف حقه فليعمل نفسه بإحكامه حالة التركيب

NASHR:v1p361/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p361/r1.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p361/r1.claim: Where lexical madd for a following hamza is stronger than semantic madd, he applies full madd and drops the weaker semantic reason for tawassut.
NASHR:v1p361/r1.anchor: واللفظي أقوى كما تقدم، فيمد له فيه مدا مشبعا على أصله في المد

NASHR:v1p361/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p361/r2.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p361/r2.claim: At a stop on words like يشاء, qasr is never allowed; nor is tawassut for a reader who uses full madd in continuation, while full madd can apply for one who uses tawassut.
NASHR:v1p361/r2.anchor: لا يجوز فيه القصر على أحد وإن كان ساكنا للوقف، وكذا لا يجوز التوسط وفقا لمن مذهبه الإشباع وصلا

NASHR:v1p361/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p361/r3.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p361/r3.claim: Warsh must use full madd on al-samāʾ because the original madd cause remains and is strengthened by stopping; al-Azraq may not use qasr at pause.
NASHR:v1p361/r3.anchor: ولو وقف مثلا عليه لورش لم يجز له غير الإشباع، ولا يجوز له ما دون ذلك من توسط أو قصر

NASHR:v1p361/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p361/r4.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p361/r4.claim: For al-Azraq on يستهزئون, متكئين, and المآب, the pause option follows the connected reading: full madd stays full, while tawassut or qasr may expand if the stopping cause is counted.
NASHR:v1p361/r4.anchor: فمن روى عنه المد وصلا وقف كذلك، سواء اعتد بالعارض، أو لم يعتد

NASHR:v1p361/r5.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p361/r5.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p361/r5.claim: Warsh reads رأى أيديهم, جاءوا أباهم, and السوءى أن كذبوا with full madd in connection; pausing before the hamza allows three options, while برآء and آمين البيت stay full.
NASHR:v1p361/r5.anchor: وصلا مد وجها واحدا مشبعا عملا بأقوى السببين، وهو المد لأجل الهمز بعد حرف المد

BURHAN:v4p431/r8.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p431/r8.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p431/r8.claim: The source lists هل ننبئكم بالأخسرين أعمالا as an example where هل is said to mean إلا.
BURHAN:v4p431/r8.anchor: وبمعنى إلا كقوله ﴿ هل ننبئكم بالأخسرين أعمالا ﴾

ITQAN:v1p259/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p259/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p259/r1.claim: Al-Hudhali assigns the sixth madd level five alifs for Hamza and the seventh, excessive level six alifs for Warsh.
ITQAN:v1p259/r1.anchor: السادسة فوق ذلك وقدرها الهذلي بخمس ألفات على تقدير الخامسة بأربع وذكر أنها لحمزة

ITQAN:v1p259/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p259/r2.speaker: ابن الجزري
ITQAN:v1p259/r2.claim: Ibn al-Jazari says counting madd levels in alifs is only verbal: each slight increase creates the next level along a continuum.
ITQAN:v1p259/r2.anchor: قال ابن الجزري وهذا الاختلاف في تقدير المراتب بالألفات لا تحقيق وراءه بل هو لفظي

ITQAN:v1p259/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p259/r3.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p259/r3.claim: For temporary madd, every reciter may choose among extension, intermediate length, and shortening.
ITQAN:v1p259/r3.anchor: وأما العارض فيجوز فيه لكل من القراء كل من الأوجه الثلاثة المد والتوسط والقصر

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p623/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p623/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p623/r1.anchor: ' هل ' حرف استفهام . قال ابن قتيبة

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p623/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p623/r2.speaker: ابن قتيبة
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p623/r2.claim: Ibn Qutayba says هل can carry the same emphatic or rebuking force as the interrogative hamza.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p623/r2.anchor: قال ابن قتيبة : ويدخلها من معنى التقرير والتوبيخ ما يدخل الألف التي يستفهم بها

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p623/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p623/r3.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p623/r3.claim: The first use is a genuine question, illustrated by questions about intercessors, guidance, shared property, and whether Hell is full.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p623/r3.anchor: أحدها : الاستفهام . ومنه قوله تعالى [ في الأعراف ] : ﴿ فهل لنا من شفعاء فيشفعوا لنا ﴾

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p623/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p623/r4.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p623/r4.claim: The second use means قد, as in the questions that introduce accounts of Moses, the disputants, Abraham's guests, the human being, and the Overwhelming Event.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p623/r4.anchor: والثاني : بمعنى ' قد ' . ومنه قوله تعالى في طه : ^ ( وهل أتاك حديث موسى ) ^

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p623/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p623/r5.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p623/r5.claim: A third use means ما, in rhetorical questions whose implied answer is negative or exclusive.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p623/r5.anchor: والثالث : بمعنى ' ما ' . ومنه قوله تعالى في البقرة : ^ ( هل ينظرون إلا أن يأتيهم الله

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p623/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p623/r6.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p623/r6.claim: The fourth use means ألا, an inviting or prompting question; the entry applies it to 18:103 and examples about guidance and trade.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p623/r6.anchor: والرابع : بمعنى ' ألا ' . ومنه قوله تعالى في الكهف : ﴿ هل ننبئكم بالأخسرين أعمالا ﴾

BURHAN:v1p130/r18.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p130/r18.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p130/r18.claim: Al-Māʾida has أنبئكم with hamza; al-Kahf has ننبئكم with nūn.
BURHAN:v1p130/r18.anchor: فى المائدة ﴿ قل هل أنبئكم ﴾ وبالنون فى الكهف

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p920/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p920/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p920/r1.claim: Nabaʾ is more momentous than khabar, and the verb anbaʾ is stronger than akhbara; broadcasters should say نشرة الأنباء for major news and نشرة الأخبار for ordinary news.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p920/r1.anchor: والصيغة الفعلية للنبأ (أنبأ) أقوى أيضاً منها للخبر (أخبر)
